title: fix(plugin-charts): the chart heading follows the viewer's language, not the author's key order (objectui#8943)
body:
Fixes #8943

`normalizeChartSchema`'s module-local `label()` resolved the inline-locale-map arm of `I18nLabel` with `Object.values(v).find(isString)` — **the first string in key order**. A chart heading therefore followed however the author happened to type the object literal rather than who was looking at it. Reordering the JSON, with no other change, showed the same viewer a different language. Deterministic, silent, no diagnostic.

`label()` now delegates to `pickLocalized` (`@object-ui/i18n`) — the repository's one answer for this union, and the pinned twin of the backend's `resolveI18nLabel`. No second resolver is minted.

---

## ⚠️ READ FIRST — this changes a PUBLISHED signature (Clause-② applies)

`normalizeChartSchema` is **not** internal to `@object-ui/plugin-charts`. It is re-exported from the package entry (`packages/plugin-charts/src/index.tsx:32`), the package declares exactly one export path (`.` to `./dist/index.d.ts`), and the built declaration moved:

| | published declaration |
|---|---|
| before (`origin/main`) | `export declare function normalizeChartSchema(schema: unknown): NormalizedChartSchema;` |
| after (this branch) | `export declare function normalizeChartSchema(schema: unknown, language?: string \| null): NormalizedChartSchema;` |

Measured on the built artifact, with a control: grepping the same `dist/normalizeChartSchema.d.ts` for the module-local helpers (`normalizeAxis`, `normalizeSeries`, `label`) returns **0**, so the hit on `normalizeChartSchema` is a real published export and not a grep that matches everything.

The change is **additive** — an optional second parameter — so every existing caller still compiles, and every non-label key of the result is byte-for-byte unchanged. But it is a public-surface change and needs the in-seat review of record before this lands. **This PR stays draft.**

Verified against the published face, both directions, from a real consumer package (`@object-ui/plugin-dashboard`, whose `tsc` resolves the specifier to `packages/plugin-charts/dist/index.d.ts` — confirmed by `--traceResolution`):

- **accept leg** — a two-argument call adds **0** errors over the package's 2-error baseline.
- **reject leg (control)** — a three-argument call errors `TS2554: Expected 1-2 arguments, but got 3`.

That diagnostic text is the load-bearing part: "1-2" is producible **only** by the rebuilt declaration. The pre-change one would have said "Expected 1 argument". So the accept leg is a reading and not a stale-cache artifact.

---

## Route taken, and why

The card named two routes and ruled that whichever is taken, `pickLocalized` must end up the single resolver.

**Route 1 — thread the language into `normalizeChartSchema`.** Taken. `label()` delegates; `ChartRenderer` reads `useObjectTranslation().language` and hands it down.

Route 2 (leave normalisation locale-free, resolve at the render site) was rejected on measurement, not taste: `NormalizedChartSchema.title` / `subtitle` / `description` and `NormalizedAxis.title` / `NormalizedSeries.label` are all declared `string`, and `NormalizedChartSchema` is published beside the function. Route 2 widens all five to the union — a **larger** public-surface change than route 1 — and moves resolution to `AdvancedChartImpl`'s ChartFrame, its axis-label prop and its series config, i.e. it multiplies read sites where route 1 keeps one. The card's own note says the same thing from the other side: "route 1 keeps one answer for every `label()` caller in the file".

No third route was invented: nothing resolves a locale locally any more.

## Every `label()` caller, none left behind

All five in the file take the language. Nothing is ledgered as skipped, because nothing was skipped:

| read site | key |
|---|---|
| `normalizeChartSchema` | `title` |
| `normalizeChartSchema` | `subtitle` |
| `normalizeChartSchema` | `description` |
| `normalizeAxis` (named by the card) | axis `title` |
| `normalizeSeries` | series `label` |

The one `normalizeChartSchema` **caller** that deliberately passes no language is `resolveChartCategoryField` (`ObjectChart.tsx`), ledgered by name in its own docblock: it reads `.xAxisKey`, a column name, and resolves no label at all, so a language argument would change no byte of its answer. It is also called from plain module scope, outside any component, where no hook is available.

## One bug the threading created, and caught

`rawSeries.map(normalizeSeries)` was point-free. `Array#map` hands its callback the **index** as the second argument — which is now `normalizeSeries`' `language`. Every series after the first would have resolved its label against `1`, `2`, … as locale tags. The call is now an arrow, and a dedicated case pins it (three series, all asserted; the point-free spelling reds there and nowhere else, because entry `0` would still be right).

## The admission test did NOT widen

`pickLocalized` alone also stringifies numbers and booleans (`String(value)`). Routing everything through it would have made the renderer accept a wider authoring surface than the contract declares. Per AGENTS.md #0.1 that belongs in the spec if it is wanted, not in a renderer-side coercion — so a guard keeps the admitted set exactly what `I18nLabel` admits, and `pickLocalized` decides only WHICH entry of an admitted value wins. Pinned: a numeric, boolean, array, empty-string and empty-object `title` are all still refused.

## Tests

Two files, and they cover different failures — the second one is not decoration, see the ablations.

- `normalizeChartSchema.localeLabel-8943.test.ts` (13 cases) — the resolver, one case per read site. **Every language assertion carries a KEY-ORDER CONTROL**: the same map written in the opposite key order, asserted to resolve identically. Without it a green is satisfiable by a resolver that still reads key order and merely happened to agree with the expected language — the exact defect, passing its own test. A plain-string title is carried through as a second control.
- `ChartRenderer.localeHeading-8943.test.tsx` (3 cases) — the card's acceptance at runtime: the same locale map, two `I18nProvider` languages, two rendered headings, plus the plain-string control. The map is written **`en` first**, the order under which the old code showed a Chinese console the English heading.

### Ablations — prediction stated first, then measured

Predictions were written down before either run. Both matched exactly; there is no miscount to report.

**A — revert `label()` to the pre-fix first-string-wins pick** (signature kept, so only the resolver is ablated).

- predicted: 11 failed tests across 2 files — 10 of 13 unit cases, 1 of 3 DOM cases; the plain-string control, the refusal case, the non-label-keys case and all 44 pre-existing `normalizeChartSchema.test.ts` cases staying green.
- measured: `Test Files 2 failed | 1 passed (3)`, `Tests 11 failed | 49 passed (60)` — the same 11 by name.

**B — leave `label()` fixed, stop `ChartRenderer` passing the language.** This is the ablation that justifies the second test file.

- predicted: the entire unit file green, exactly 1 DOM case red.
- measured: `Test Files 1 failed | 1 passed (2)`, `Tests 1 failed | 15 passed (16)` — the failure being "renders the zh-CN entry to a zh-CN viewer".

⇒ a resolver-only fix that forgets the plumbing passes **every** unit test and still paints the wrong heading. That is the case the DOM pin exists for.

Both ablations are one-shot: each mutated from the committed fix, proved the mutation reached disk before believing the run (injected-marker count, deleted-line count, and a `git hash-object` that differs from the `HEAD` blob — an editor's exit code is not evidence, `sed`/`perl -i`/`str.replace` all exit 0 on zero matches), then restored with `git checkout HEAD -- PATH` under a `trap`. Restoration was verified byte-identical (`git hash-object` equals the `HEAD` blob, marker count back to 0, `git status --porcelain` empty), not by a return code. No ablation artefact is committed.

No rebuild leg is part of either ablation, and that is measured rather than assumed: both pins import the module under test through a **relative** specifier (`./normalizeChartSchema`, `./ChartRenderer`), so they read `src/`, not `dist/`.

### Verification run

| what | result |
|---|---|
| `pnpm exec vitest run packages/plugin-charts/` | `Test Files 57 passed (57)`, `Tests 524 passed (524)` |
| `pnpm --filter @object-ui/plugin-charts type-check` | exit 0 — and `tsc -p tsconfig.test.json --listFiles` confirms **both** new test files are in the typechecked set, so this is coverage and not a silent exclusion |
| dependency-closure build (`--filter '@object-ui/plugin-charts^...'`) | exit 0 |
| `pnpm --filter @object-ui/plugin-charts lint` | exit 0 (0 errors, 362 warnings — the package's standing warning level) |
| repo-wide `eslint . --no-inline-config --format json` | 4756 files linted, 79 files carry errors, **0 of them in `packages/plugin-charts`**; every file this PR touches reports `errorCount: 0`. eslint here is not type-aware (no `projectService` and no `parserOptions.project` in `eslint.config.js`, control-checked against a pattern that does hit that file), so this diff cannot move the verdict of a file it did not touch |
| cross-package consumer `DatasetWidget.comboPresentation.test.tsx` | 12 passed — the one out-of-package caller of the symbol, calling it with one argument |
| `check:control-bytes`, `check:phantom-deps`, `check:unused-deps`, `check:self-import`, `check:vi-mock-specifiers`, `check:vi-mock-inherit`, `check:vi-mock-override-shape`, `check:new-line-citations`, `check:pre-install-import-graph`, `check:unreferenced-sources`, `check:docs-route-closure`, `check:changeset-presence`, `check:changeset-no-major`, `check:governed-queue-guard --test` | all exit 0 |

Control-byte self-scan over every changed file returns no hits.

**NOT MEASURED locally, with reasons — both are repo-scoped gates CI owns, and neither failed on this diff:**

- `check:eager-closure` — exits 2 with "No eager-closure report at `apps/console/dist/eager-closure.json`", which the gate itself calls a broken gauge rather than a pass. The report is written by the `apps/console` production build in `performance-budget.yml`. It is nonetheless the gate most obviously implicated here, since this adds an eager `@object-ui/i18n` import to two modules — so the structural half was measured directly on `origin/main`: the package entry statically re-exports `./ObjectChart` (`index.tsx:16`) and `ObjectChart.tsx:9` statically imports the `@object-ui/i18n` barrel, with zero dynamic-import spellings on either. `@object-ui/i18n` was therefore **already** in that entry's eager closure before this change, and these imports add no module to it.
- `check:readme-exports` — exits 1 on "27 unbuilt" of 40 tracked packages, i.e. it needs a full-monorepo build. Building `@object-ui/plugin-charts` moved it from 9 to 10 built packages; the remaining shortfall is a prerequisite, not a finding, and no message names a file this PR touches.

## Acceptance notes

**Reach limit of this fix, stated plainly.** On the dataset path an axis title is collapsed to a string by `axisPresentation`/`labelText` in `@object-ui/core` **before** `normalizeChartSchema` ever sees it, so `normalizeAxis`'s new language-awareness cannot help that path. That first-string-wins pick is deliberate, documented in the file, and ledgered against objectui#4020 (the package is React-free and holds no provider, and the design is that a caller which CAN resolve the language overrides the merged label). Noted, not filed — it is a recorded decision, not a fresh finding, and reopening it is a contract decision of its own.

**Filed:** objectui#9038 — the neighbouring limb in the same `@object-ui/core` file, `chartConfigPresentation`'s `text()`, is a different failure and is **not** covered by that ledger: it does not make a locale-unaware pick a caller can override, it **erases** a locale-map `title`/`subtitle`/`description` outright, so a dashboard or report chart authored in the spec's own `I18nLabel` union renders with no heading at all and nothing survives for any caller to re-resolve. Both call sites were measured, and both already hold a language.

**Noted, not filed** — `normalizeChartSchema.test.ts`'s existing locale-map case asserts only `typeof out.title === 'string'` and truthiness, so it passes both before and after and pins nothing about which entry wins. It is left alone rather than rewritten: the new file pins that property properly and this one still covers the union collapsing to a string. Successor: whoever next touches that file. It required no fixture triage — no fixture in the repo pinned the key-order behaviour, so nothing needed re-judging.

Out of scope and untouched, per the card: objectui#7946 / PR objectui#8884's ruled key set.

## Serial adjacency

Re-derived against the live open-PR list at the moment work started (11 open PRs), not from the dispatch's snapshot. Of those, the ones touching anything near this diff:

- **objectui#8941** — `packages/plugin-charts/package.json` (a `lucide-react` range bump). **No conflict:** this PR changes no manifest. `@object-ui/i18n` was already a declared `workspace:*` dependency of `@object-ui/plugin-charts`, so nothing here adds a dependency edge.
- **objectui#9021 / objectui#9017 / objectui#9028** — `packages/types/**` only. No overlap.
- **objectui#9016** — already merged (it is this branch's base, `681d3f10e`), so its `ObjectChart.tsx` changes are included rather than pending.

No open PR touches `packages/plugin-charts/src/**`.

## Housekeeping

The card carried no assignee when this seat received it, and it was worked without one.
